summary.headline: Clean Science Q1 FY27 consolidated sales hit a record INR264 crore (+10% YoY, +7% QoQ), with standalone EBITDA at INR87 crore (43% margin).
summary.overview: Management reported record consolidated sales of about INR264 crore, up 7% QoQ and 10% YoY, driven by HALS scale-up. Standalone revenue rose 5% QoQ to INR203 crore on realisation gains, while standalone sales fell 6% YoY on volume loss from raw-material and shipping disruptions, including about two weeks of production stoppage. HALS is now 22% of sales and legacy top-4 products fell to 60% of sales from 85% in Q4 FY23. Management announced a Geneus Chem (Swiss) collaboration for advanced NOR HALS and a 5-year Kemin supply contract, and said CFCL became operationally self-sustaining.

financial_highlights.change: 43% margin; c.+5% vs adjusted Q4 FY26 EBITDA of c.INR83 crore
36% margin; c.+37% vs adjusted Q4 FY26 PAT of c.INR53 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Top-4 legacy products share of sales

segments.name: HALS (CFCL / Clean Fino-Chem subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Volume about 1,000 tonnes in Q1; average realisation up from about INR440/kg to INR550/kg as mix moved to higher grades. Exports about 50% of HALS sales versus fully domestic in the first year. Annualised HALS revenue guided at INR250-300 crore.

segments.name: Performance Chemicals (hydroquinone and catechol, PC1)
segments.commentary: Stabilisation largely complete and customer approvals received; commercial revenue expected from August-September 2026 with a gradual ramp.

segments.name: Performance Chemicals 2 (PC2)
segments.commentary: Commercialisation now expected around November 2026 after labour-related delay; major revenue expected from Q1 FY28. Management said about INR100 crore was infused into the subsidiary in Q1, taking total investment to about INR850 crore.

guidance_outlook: HALS revenue targeted at INR250-300 crore for FY27, about 30-35% of overall revenue growth; FY28 HALS guidance not yet given.
Management expects EBITDA margins to keep improving as mix shifts to higher-grade HALS.

Geneus Chem NOR HALS tech transfer: plant to start in Q3 FY27; partnership expected to add INR300-350 crore cumulative revenue over 3-4 years, with peak year around INR100 crore plus or minus (per analyst's reading, confirmed as possible).
Kemin: offtake expected to rise 20-40%, starting in the next 2-3 months; additional capacity required and process started.
All new products and lines to be housed in Clean Fino-Chem (CFCL). Europe subsidiary in the Netherlands to start mid-September 2026.
Price increases may be limited going forward; management said price increases 'might be a big question'.
capex_capacity: HALS capacity about 10,000 tonnes; split roughly 40% lower grade and 60% higher grade.
Geneus Chem NOR HALS is a new setup with new technology; capex about INR25 crore; production expected Q3 FY27.
Kemin deal requires additional capacity; capex not yet quantified, described as 'not going to be too much'.
PC2 to start around November-December 2026; Q3-Q4 for line setup and quality; major revenue from Q1 FY28.
Subsidiary capital infusion of about INR100 crore in Q1; total investment about INR850 crore.
demand_pricing: Standalone QoQ revenue growth was driven by realisation increases across all products; volumes were flat QoQ, with YoY decline from supply-side disruptions.
Management said demand is steady. Standalone YoY volume loss was from about two weeks of shutdown at a primary Indian supplier that lacked propylene.

Input cost increases from Middle East crisis were only partly passed on, with some long-term contracts limiting pass-through. Management said end-product prices remain stable and competitive intensity unchanged 'at the moment'.
HALS competitors: BASF and Sabo in Europe; Rianlon and Suqian (Unitechem) in China.
Management said NOR HALS market is currently dominated by BASF; Geneus-linked products to be co-branded and jointly marketed with geographic split.
Other expenses up about 13% QoQ at consolidated level due to higher Q4 CSR spend and provisions reversal; management said Q1 is a sustainable base.

qa_highlights.question: What drove HALS volume and pricing, and is the INR250-300 crore annual run-rate comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume about 1,000 tonnes in Q1; average price rose from about INR440 to INR550/kg on mix shift (HALS 770 share fell from about 50% to 35%). Management said the INR250-300 crore annualised run-rate is comfortable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 43-45% HALS gross margin sustainable, or helped by cheap acetone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no real benefit from cheap raw material; margins came from higher grades and operational efficiencies, and should be sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Geneus Chem transaction and its revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech transfer for NOR HALS with no transfer fee or royalty (capex only); joint, co-branded marketing with geographic split. Management guided INR300-350 crore additional revenue cumulatively over 3-4 years, separate from direct sales outside the partner.

qa_highlights.question: What was the cause of the YoY decline in legacy volumes, and will volumes recover in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Propylene shortage at a primary Indian supplier forced about two weeks of shutdown. Management said volumes are not an issue now; raw material pricing and shipping availability remain challenges.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Kemin 5-year contract add volume and need capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kemin is an existing 10-year customer; offtake expected to rise 20-40% starting in 2-3 months. Additional capacity is needed and the process has started; the benefit is supply security rather than pricing concessions.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Kemin and Geneus deals preempt new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no other Indian or global entrant is likely to enter this alliance given supply security, and that the contract covers BHA, BHT, TBHQ and AP.

qa_highlights.question: Is PC2 on track for September start and what is the ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said labour issues cause a delay; commercialisation expected around November, with stabilisation November-March and revenue from Q1 FY28.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility from the Middle East crisis; management said price increases 'might be a big question' and long-term contracts limit pass-through of input cost increases.
Shipping vessel availability and propylene supply for primary Indian supplier; management said availability has improved but RM pricing remains an issue.
PC2 commercialisation slipped to around November 2026 after labour-related delay; stabilisation November-March and major revenue only from Q1 FY28.
HALS FY27 target of INR250-300 crore annualised; the FY28 HALS outlook has not been given yet and management said it would come back later.
Kemin and Geneus deals need additional capacity and capex; Kemin capex not quantified ('not going to be too much'), Geneus capex about INR25 crore, production expected Q3 FY27.

Geneus NOR HALS incremental revenue of INR300-350 crore cumulative over 3-4 years; peak year around INR100 crore described as 'Possible' by management, and direct sales outside the partner are incremental.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on HALS scale-up, margins and the Kemin and Geneus deals, but cautious on pricing and supply chain. On price increases, Siddharth Sikchi said they might be "a big question", and on supply stability he was not "so confident that it is locked". Capex and FY28 HALS numbers were left open ("we will come back to you").
